evidence.says: Sara E. Wermiel is listed as the author of The Fireproof Building (2000).
Sara E. Wermiel wrote the 1997 Business History Review review of Safety First.

basis: The sources give the same full name for the book author and reviewer, but the permitted evidence located does not independently link both works to one person.

evidence.says: Thomas Ott reviewed Dietmar Heil's Die Reichspolitik Bayerns in 2000.
Thomas Ott earned a Tennessee Ph.D. in 1970 and published The Haitian Revolution in 1973; he taught at the University of North Alabama.
Thomas Ott's Präzedenz und Nachbarschaft was a dissertation accepted at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich in 2005/06.

basis: The sources identify two scholars named Thomas Ott with different doctorates, but do not establish that the Munich scholar wrote the review on side a. The review's subject alone cannot establish that identification.

evidence.says: John H. Hepp IV lists The Middle-Class City and H-Net book reviews in 2014, without identifying their titles.
John Henry Hepp IV wrote The Middle-Class City and taught history at Wilkes University.

basis: The CV places the author of the book on side b among H-Net reviewers in 2014, but does not identify the particular review on side a. The available evidence does not establish that the two keys are the same person.

evidence.says: The 2012 review of Busse's Engagement oder Rückzug? is catalogued under Stefan L. Wolff.
Stefan L. Wolff was born in 1952 and received a doctorate in the history of physics at Munich in 1988.
Stefan Wolff, born in 1969, edited German Minorities in Europe and was a professor at the University of Birmingham.

basis: The review is catalogued under Stefan L. Wolff, the historian of physics born in 1952. The editor of German Minorities in Europe was born in 1969, indicating two distinct scholars.

evidence.says: Judy Kutulas wrote The Long War and is an assistant professor of history at St. Olaf College.

basis: The publisher's distributor identifies the author of a work on side a, but the available sources did not establish a link to the review on side b. The H-Net review page could not be accessed.

evidence.says: Bernard Mandel wrote Labor, Free and Slave and a biography of Samuel Gompers.
A review identifies the author of Labor, Free and Slave as Bernard Mandel, who held a doctorate from Case Western Reserve University.

basis: The book author held a doctorate, but the available evidence does not identify the institution of the 1952 thesis or connect that thesis to the book. The shared name and subject alone do not establish identity.

evidence.says: Tobias Straumann authored the 2010 report on the conference Krisen - Ursachen, Deutungen und Folgen.
Tobias Straumann's publications include Fixed Ideas of Money and the 2012 volume Krisen: Ursachen, Deutungen und Folgen.

basis: The author of the report and the author of Fixed Ideas of Money share a name, and the latter edited a volume associated with the conference. The sources do not directly identify the report's author with the book's author or give the report author's affiliation, so the required identity link remains unconfirmed.

evidence.says: Cites John L. Tone's 1989 Columbia Ph.D. dissertation, The Fatal Knot: Popular Resistance and Guerrilla Warfare in Navarre, 1808–1814.
Names John Tone as author of the forthcoming book The Fatal Knot and an assistant professor at Georgia Tech.

basis: A 1989 dissertation and the book have closely related titles, but the dissertation is cited under a different title from the thesis on key b. The sources found do not establish that the two dissertation titles refer to the same work.

evidence.says: Christine R. Johnson reviewed Haut zwischen 1500 und 1800 for H-German in January 2004; the review gives no affiliation.
Christine Johnson is an associate professor of history at Washington University and author of The German Discovery of the World.

basis: The review identifies its author by name but gives no affiliation or other fact linking her to the author of the book. The shared name and subject do not establish identity.

evidence.says: David Stebenne has taught at Ohio State since 1993 and wrote Arthur J. Goldberg: New Deal Liberal and Modern Republican.

basis: Ohio State identifies the author of works on side b, but the available evidence did not establish the affiliation or other works of the reviewer on side a. The shared name and subject do not establish identity.

evidence.says: Cites Martin Pine's Pietro Pomponazzi and the Immortality Controversy, 1516–1524 as a 1965 Columbia University thesis.
Lists Martin Pine's Pietro Pomponazzi: Radical Philosopher of the Renaissance (1986).

basis: The records share a name and closely related subject, but the sources found do not establish that the 1986 book's author wrote the 1965 thesis or that the book grew out of it. The evidence therefore does not meet the required identity standard.

evidence.says: Tufts lists Philip Edward Burnham Jr., Harvard BA, with the history dissertation Cultural Life at Papal Avignon, 1309-1376.
Philip Edward Burnham Jr. received a 1972 Tufts PhD in medieval studies and taught history in New England.
The author of Indian Country, God's Country and Song of Dewey Beard lists a Beloit BA and a New Mexico PhD in American Studies.

basis: The Tufts dissertation belongs to Philip Edward Burnham Jr., a Harvard graduate and history teacher. The author of the books lists a different undergraduate degree, doctorate, and career, indicating two people.

evidence.says: Hugh Rockoff lists a 1973 review of Finance and Economic Development in the Old South by George Green.
The 1989 University of Texas at Arlington history faculty list includes professor George N. Green.

basis: The sources identify the author of the book and a Texas historian, but do not establish whether either is the reviewer or whether they are different people. The institutional clues alone do not settle the identity of the two keys.

James D. Norris was a history professor at Northern Illinois University and wrote Frontier Iron and R.G. Dun & Co.

basis: The graph records separate AHA doctoral entries for the 1961 Maramec dissertation and the 1971 Geneva Protocol dissertation. The Ohio History source independently identifies the Maramec work as James D. Norris's doctoral dissertation; the separate doctorates indicate different scholars, although the Geneva record was not independently corroborated.

evidence.says: Kathleen Coyne Kelly wrote A. S. Byatt and Performing Virginity and earned a PhD at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill in 1990.
Kathleen Kelly's Maryknoll in Manchuria is listed as a 1982 PhD dissertation at Southern California.

basis: The works are associated with different doctorates at different universities, in 1982 and 1990. The distinct doctoral careers support treating these as different scholars.

evidence.says: Lists Ralf Ptak's review of Iris Karabelas, Freiheit statt Sozialismus, dated 9 February 2012.
Lists Ralf Ptak as author of Vom Ordoliberalismus zur Sozialen Marktwirtschaft and identifies an affiliation with the University of Cologne.

basis: The sources identify the reviewer and the book's author, but do not establish a link between their works or careers. The shared name and subject alone do not establish identity.

evidence.says: John Hepp reviewed Nature's Entrepôt for H-SHEAR in May 2015; the review gives no affiliation.
John Hepp is an associate professor of history at Wilkes University.

basis: The review does not identify its author by institution or link him to the other key's works. The shared name and field are insufficient to establish identity.

evidence.says: British Rational Secularism is listed under Walter David Nelson, Washington, June 1964.
A reference identifies Walter David Nelson's British Rational Secularism as a University of Washington PhD thesis, 1963.
Small Wonder is listed under Walter Henry Nelson, with a 1965 publication date.
A review identifies Walter Henry Nelson, author of The Great Discount Delusion, as having worked for ten years in advertising, public relations and manufacturing.

basis: The dissertation is attributed to Walter David Nelson, while the books are by Walter Henry Nelson. Their distinct middle names and the book author's contemporaneous career support treating them as different people; the conclusion is inferred rather than explicitly stated by a source.

evidence.says: Lists Matthias Frese’s 2012 H-Soz-u-Kult review of David Templin’s Lehrzeit – keine Leerzeit!.
Identifies Matthias Frese of the LWL regional history institute as author of Betriebspolitik im „Dritten Reich“ (1991).

basis: The review listing identifies its author by name, while the institute report identifies the author of the book. The sources do not establish that the reviewer and book author are the same person.

evidence.says: Middlesex University Press published Laurence Cole's Dusty Springfield: In the Middle of Nowhere in 2008.
Laurence Cole of the University of Salzburg edited Different Paths to the Nation and co-edited The Limits of Loyalty.
Laurence Cole's CV lists Birkbeck College, University of London, in 1997–1999 and 2000–2001.

basis: The sources identify the works and establish the historian's Birkbeck affiliation, but do not connect the music book to that historian or establish that the authors are different people. The pair should remain separate pending decisive evidence.

evidence.says: Lists Paul Dean Lack's Urban Slavery in the Southwest as a 1973 Texas Tech University dissertation.
Paul D. Lack served McMurry from 1971 to 2002 and authored The Texas Revolutionary Experience.
Paul Lack, author of The Texas Revolutionary Experience, received a Texas Tech history department alumnus award in 1993.

basis: The book's author was a Texas Tech alumnus, and the dissertation was submitted there in 1973. The sources do not establish that the book's author was at Texas Tech in 1973 or directly link him to the dissertation.

evidence.says: Catalogues The Scots in Australia (1983) under Malcolm D. (Malcolm David) Prentis.

basis: The catalogue identifies the author of the 1983 book, but no source found connects that author to the 2001 review. The shared name and subject alone do not establish identity.

evidence.says: Jonathan W. White reviewed Deserter Country for H-CivWar in April 2010; the review gives no affiliation.
Jonathan W. White wrote Abraham Lincoln and Treason in the Civil War and is identified with Christopher Newport University.

basis: The review and book share an author name, but the sources found do not connect the reviewer to the book or to the institution. The shared subject alone does not establish identity.

evidence.says: UW–Madison lists Peter Williams, The Construction of Versailles, 1661-1715, among its 1977–1978 history doctorates.
The 1977 publication of The Construction of Versailles names its author Peter William Williams.
Peter W. Williams is identified with Miami University.

basis: The Versailles dissertation author is Peter William Williams, but the sources found do not establish a link to the Miami University scholar or demonstrate that they are different people. The shared name and differing subjects alone do not decide identity.

evidence.says: Karim Michel Tiro lists The People of the Standing Stone, reviews in H-AmIndian, and a Xavier history appointment from 1999.

basis: The CV connects the book and reviews in the same venue, but does not identify the 2008 Forgotten Allies review specifically. The available evidence does not establish that review author’s identity beyond the shared name.

evidence.says: The catalogue credits Philip Garone with the December 2011 H-Net review of How Local Politics Shape Federal Policy.
The university compendium lists Philip Garone in History and his 2014 response on The Fall and Rise of the Wetlands of California’s Great Central Valley.

basis: The sources identify the reviewer and the wetlands book author, but do not establish a link between them or place the reviewer at the same institution. The shared name and subject alone do not establish identity.

evidence.says: The Library of Congress identifies Robert R. King as Robert Ray King, born 1942.
Florida State University's bibliography attributes The Florida Seminole Polity to Robert T. King, University of Florida, 1978.
The bibliography attributes A History of the Romanian Communist Party (1980) to Robert R. King.

basis: The dissertation is attributed to Robert T. King, while the other key is the Library of Congress's Robert R. (Robert Ray) King. The incompatible middle initials and overlapping publication years support two different people.

evidence.says: John C. Wills, The Politics of Taste in the New Republic, University of Michigan, 1994.
John Wills, ORCID 0000-0001-8517-3207, studied for his MA and PhD at Bristol and wrote Disney Culture and Gamer Nation.

basis: The Philadelphia dissertation is attributed to John C. Wills at Michigan, while Kent's profile identifies the author of the other key's books as having a Bristol PhD. The different doctorates and the Kent profile's account of his education support separate identities; the inference allows for the possibility of an unlisted additional degree.

evidence.says: The library attributes the 1949 Chinese Revolution dissertation to James William Moran.
A dissertation bibliography lists James W. Moran’s Chinese Revolution thesis as a 1949 Colorado PhD.
The catalogue lists Printing presses and Clays of Bungay under James Moran.

basis: The sources identify the dissertation author as James William Moran, but do not connect him to the printing historian or establish incompatible careers. The shared name alone is insufficient to merge the keys.

evidence.says: Michael Wayne Cole is the author of Cellini and the Principles of Sculpture (2002).
Michael Wayne Cole was a Princeton art history dissertation fellow in 1998–1999, with a dissertation on Benvenuto Cellini.
Michael S. Cole was a 2012 thesis committee member at Florida Gulf Coast University in history.

basis: The author of the Cellini book had a Princeton art history dissertation, while the other key has a 2003 dissertation in history and a Florida Gulf Coast affiliation. The institution identifies its historian as Michael S. Cole, supporting distinct careers and different middle initials.

evidence.says: Brian T. Cannon authored An Enduring Prestige: Land Grants in a Princely State Census (2023).
In 2021 Brian T. Cannon was a PhD candidate at the University of Pennsylvania.
Brian Q. Cannon is a BYU history professor and author of Remaking the Agrarian Dream.
BYU lists Brian Q. Cannon as professor, with a 1992 PhD from the University of Wisconsin.

basis: Brian T. Cannon was a Pennsylvania doctoral candidate in 2021, while Brian Q. Cannon had earned a Wisconsin doctorate in 1992 and held a BYU professorship. Their distinct initials and overlapping career stages support two different scholars.

evidence.says: University Press of Florida lists Slavery and Salvation in Colonial Cartagena de Indias by Margaret M. Olsen.
Cites One Nation, One World by Margaret Nunnelley Olsen as a Rice University thesis.

basis: The sources identify the authors of the book and thesis but do not establish a link or a decisive difference between them. The works' different subjects alone do not establish two people.

evidence.says: Jane McLeod is an associate professor of history at Brock University and has Licensing Loyalty in press.

basis: The source identifies the book's author, but the sources found do not establish that she wrote the 1987 thesis. The shared name and subject alone are insufficient to merge the keys.

evidence.says: Katherine S. Van Eerde taught history at Muhlenberg College and received a Ph.D. from Yale in 1945.

basis: The 1945 doctorate and Muhlenberg affiliation match the respective records, but the available evidence does not identify the thesis or its institution and so does not establish a link between the two keys.

evidence.says: Jorge Eduardo Myers is a professor at Universidad Nacional de Quilmes and is listed as author of Orden y virtud (1995).
Jorge Myers wrote In Memoriam: J. G. A. Pocock and the History of Discourses of Politics.

basis: The sources identify the authors of the two works but do not establish a shared institutional affiliation or explicitly link the works to one person. The similarity of names and subject matter alone is insufficient to establish identity.

evidence.says: Joy Jackson's papers include a manuscript of New Orleans in the Gilded Age and Tulane commencement material from 1961.

basis: The archive connects the book author to Tulane in 1961, but the available evidence does not identify the dissertation on the other key or connect it to the book. The shared name, year and subject alone do not establish identity.

evidence.says: Thomas Ott reviewed Der Kurfürstentag zu Frankfurt 1558 und der Reichstag zu Augsburg 1559 and was affiliated with the historical seminar at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich.
Thomas Ott's Präzedenz und Nachbarschaft was a dissertation accepted in Munich in the winter semester of 2005/2006.
Thomas Oliver Ott authored The Haitian Revolution, earned a PhD at Tennessee, and retired from the University of North Alabama in 2010.
Thomas Oliver Ott III's dissertation The Haitian Revolution, 1789-1804 is listed at the University of Tennessee in 1970.

basis: The Munich reviewer is plausibly the author of the later Munich dissertation, while the Haitian Revolution author had a separate Tennessee doctorate and a career at North Alabama. These overlapping institutional careers support two people, though the identification of the reviewer with the Munich dissertation author is inferred.

evidence.says: Ronald Lee Miller wrote Henry Delano Fitch: A Yankee Trader in California: 1826–1849, a University of Southern California dissertation in 1972.
Input–Output Analysis: Foundations and Extensions is by Ronald E. Miller and Peter D. Blair; Miller is emeritus professor of regional science at Pennsylvania.
The MIT Press catalogue credits Domestic Airline Efficiency: An Application of Linear Programming to Ronald E. Miller.

basis: The Fitch dissertation is credited to Ronald Lee Miller, while the works on the other key are credited to Ronald E. Miller. The distinct middle initials and contemporaneous work in history and regional economics strongly indicate different scholars.

evidence.says: Lists Kirwin Shaffer as author of Anarchists of the Caribbean (2020).

basis: The source confirms a work on side a, but the searches did not find a source linking it or its author to a review or affiliation on side b. The shared name and subject alone do not establish identity.

evidence.says: Jonathan Wright was Tutor in Politics at Christ Church, 1969–2009, and wrote Above Parties and Gustav Stresemann.
A review of Reformation and the Culture of Persuasion is attributed to Jonathan Wright, H-Net.
Jonathan Wright is an independent scholar and author of God's Soldiers and Shapers of the Great Debate on Freedom of Religion.
